lessons.title: Calculating Cost per Unit for Oils and Incense
lessons.body: To price your products profitably, you must first know exactly what each unit costs you to make. For perfume oils, start by listing every ingredient: carrier oils (like jojoba or sweet almond), fragrance oils or essential oils, and any additives like vitamin E. Suppose you buy 1 litre of jojoba oil for 5,000 KES. If you use 10 ml per 30 ml bottle, that's 50 KES of jojoba. Your fragrance oil costs 8,000 KES for 500 ml; using 5 ml per bottle costs 80 KES. The bottle, cap, and label cost 60 KES. So total cost per unit = 50 + 80 + 60 = 190 KES. For incense, calculate cost per stick or per bundle. If you make 100 sticks from 500 g of charcoal powder (cost 800 KES), 100 g of binder (200 KES), and 20 ml of fragrance oil (600 KES), total materials = 1,600 KES. Add 100 KES for bamboo sticks. That's 1,700 KES for 100 sticks, so 17 KES per stick. If you sell bundles of 20 sticks, cost per bundle = 340 KES. Always include a small percentage for waste or spillageâsay 5%. So for oils, add 5% of 190 = 9.5 KES, making unit cost 199.5 KES. Round up to 200 KES. For incense, add 5% to 17 = 0.85 KES, so 17.85 KES per stick. Keep a notebook or a simple Excel sheet listing all raw materials and their costs. Update prices whenever you buy new supplies. This simple step prevents you from selling at a loss. Many beginners forget to include the cost of small items like pipettes or gloves, but those add up. Track everything. Once you know your true cost per unit, you can set a price that covers costs and leaves profit.

lessons.title: Setting Wholesale and Retail Prices
lessons.body: Once you know your cost per unit, you can set two prices: wholesale (for bulk buyers like shops) and retail (for individual customers). A common rule is to double your cost for wholesale and triple it for retail. Using the perfume oil example: cost per unit = 200 KES. Wholesale price = 400 KES. Retail price = 600 KES. For incense sticks: cost per stick = 17.85 KES. Wholesale price per stick = 36 KES (if sold in bundles of 20, that's 720 KES per bundle). Retail price per stick = 54 KES (or 1,080 KES per bundle of 20). But these are just starting points. Check what competitors charge. In Nairobi, a 30 ml perfume oil might retail for 500â800 KES. If your quality is higher, you can charge more. For wholesale, offer a discount for larger orders. For example, if a shop buys 50 bottles, give them 350 KES per bottle instead of 400. That encourages bigger orders. Also consider your market: tourists might pay more, while local repeat customers expect fair prices. Always communicate your prices clearly. Write them on a price list. For retail, you can set a recommended price and let resellers add their own markup. For example, you sell wholesale at 400 KES, and suggest they retail at 600 KES. That gives them a 200 KES profit per bottle. For incense, if you sell a bundle of 20 sticks wholesale at 720 KES, suggest retail at 1,080 KES. This makes your product attractive to shops. Remember, your prices must cover all costs and leave you a profit. If you sell wholesale at double cost, your profit margin is 50% (since cost is half of selling price). That's a good target. Adjust based on what the market will bear. Test different prices at local markets and see what sells best.

lessons.title: Accounting for Packaging, Labor, and Overhead
lessons.body: Many small producers forget to include packaging, labor, and overhead in their costs, and end up losing money. Let's break these down. Packaging: For perfume oils, you need bottles, caps, labels, and maybe a box. A 30 ml glass bottle with cap might cost 50 KES, a label 10 KES, and a small gift box 30 KES. That's 90 KES per unit. If you use a cheaper plastic bottle (20 KES) and no box, packaging drops to 30 KES. For incense, packaging might be a cellophane bag and a sticker: 5 KES per bundle. Labor: Even if you work alone, your time has value. If you make 20 perfume oils in 2 hours, and you want to earn 200 KES per hour, that's 400 KES labor for 20 units = 20 KES per unit. For incense, if you make 100 sticks in 1 hour and want 150 KES per hour, that's 1.5 KES per stick. Overhead: These are ongoing costs like rent, electricity, internet, and transport. If your monthly overhead is 10,000 KES and you produce 500 units per month, overhead per unit = 20 KES. For incense, if you produce 2,000 sticks, overhead per stick = 5 KES. Now add these to your material cost. Perfume oil: materials 200 + packaging 90 + labor 20 + overhead 20 = 330 KES per unit. Incense stick: materials 17.85 + packaging 0.25 (5 KES per bundle of 20) + labor 1.5 + overhead 5 = 24.6 KES. Now your wholesale price should be at least double that: 660 KES for oil, 49 KES per stick (or 980 KES per bundle). Retail triple: 990 KES for oil, 74 KES per stick (1,480 KES per bundle). These numbers show why ignoring these costs leads to underpricing. Keep a simple notebook to track all expenses, even small ones like glue or tape.

lessons.title: Offering Discounts and Bulk Deals
lessons.body: Discounts and bulk deals can boost sales, but you must structure them so you still make a profit. First, know your break-even point. If your total cost per perfume oil is 330 KES, you cannot sell below that. For bulk deals, offer a lower price per unit but require a minimum order. For example, retail price is 990 KES. For orders of 10â19 bottles, offer 10% off: 891 KES each. For 20â49 bottles, 20% off: 792 KES each. For 50+ bottles, 30% off: 693 KES each. Check that even at 30% off, you still cover cost (330 KES) and make profit (363 KES per bottle). For incense, if cost per stick is 24.6 KES, retail 74 KES. Bulk: 10 bundles (200 sticks) at 10% off = 66.6 KES per stick; 50 bundles at 20% off = 59.2 KES per stick; 100 bundles at 30% off = 51.8 KES per stick. All are above cost. You can also offer free delivery for bulk orders within your city. Another strategy: 'Buy 5 get 1 free' for retail. If you sell 5 at 990 KES, you get 4,950 KES. Giving one free costs you 330 KES, so total revenue 4,950 for 6 units, average 825 KES per unit. That's still profitable (cost 330). But be careful: free items should not exceed your profit margin. Always calculate. Use a simple formula: Discounted price = Original price Ã (1 â discount rate). Ensure discounted price > total cost. Also, consider seasonal discounts during holidays or for loyal customers. Keep records of all discounts given so you can see if they increase sales enough to justify lower margins. Many African markets respond well to 'wholesale price' when buying in bulk, so label your deals clearly.

lessons.title: Tracking Expenses with a Simple Notebook or App
lessons.body: Tracking every expense is the only way to know if you're making a profit. You don't need fancy software; a simple notebook works. Divide a page into columns: Date, Item, Cost, Quantity, Total. For example: 1/5/2025, Jojoba oil, 5,000 KES, 1 litre. 2/5/2025, Fragrance oil, 8,000 KES, 500 ml. 3/5/2025, Bottles, 1,500 KES, 30 bottles. At the end of each week, add up all expenses. Also record sales: Date, Product, Quantity, Price per unit, Total. At month's end, subtract total expenses from total sales to get profit. If you prefer digital, use a free app like 'Expense Manager' or 'Wave' (for invoicing). Even Google Sheets on your phone works. Create a simple spreadsheet with two tabs: Expenses and Sales. For expenses, list categories: Raw Materials, Packaging, Labor, Overhead, Transport, Miscellaneous. For sales, list each transaction. The key is consistency: record every purchase and sale, no matter how small. A 50 KES pack of stickers matters. At the end of each month, calculate your cost per unit again using actual expenses. You might find that your cost per unit has changed. Adjust your prices accordingly. Also, track your inventory: how many bottles or sticks you have left. This helps you plan purchases and avoid overstocking. Many African entrepreneurs use a 'cash book' where they note all money in and out. That's enough. If you have a smartphone, apps like 'Keeper' or 'QuickBooks Self-Employed' can help, but a notebook is fine. The goal is to know your numbers so you can make smart decisions.

lessons.title: Determining Profit Margins for Growth
lessons.body: Profit margin is the percentage of each sale that is profit. It tells you how much room you have to grow. Calculate it as: (Selling Price â Total Cost) / Selling Price Ã 100. For perfume oil with total cost 330 KES and retail price 990 KES: profit = 660 KES. Margin = 660/990 Ã 100 = 66.7%. For wholesale at 660 KES: profit = 330 KES, margin = 50%. For incense stick cost 24.6 KES, retail 74 KES: profit = 49.4 KES, margin = 66.8%. Wholesale at 49 KES: profit = 24.4 KES, margin = 49.8%. These are healthy margins. But you need to consider volume. If you sell 100 oils retail, profit = 66,000 KES. If you sell 200 wholesale, profit = 66,000 KES. Same profit, but more work. So decide your strategy: high margin, low volume (retail) or lower margin, high volume (wholesale). For growth, aim for a net profit margin of at least 20â30% after all expenses. Use your profit to reinvest: buy better packaging, more raw materials, or market your products. For example, if you make 50,000 KES profit in a month, save 30% (15,000 KES) for business growth, and take 70% as your income. As you grow, you can negotiate better prices for supplies, reducing your cost per unit and increasing margin. Also, track your profit margin monthly. If it drops, find out why: maybe raw material prices increased, or you gave too many discounts. Adjust prices or cut costs. Remember, profit is not just for spending; it's for growing your business. Set a goal: e.g., increase profit margin by 5% in three months by buying in bulk. With consistent tracking and smart pricing, you can build a sustainable perfume and incense business.

quiz.q: What is the first step in calculating cost per unit for perfume oils?
options: B) List all ingredients and their costs
quiz.explanation: You must know the cost of each ingredient to calculate total unit cost.

quiz.q: If you buy 1 litre of jojoba oil for 5,000 KES and use 10 ml per 30 ml bottle, what is the jojoba cost per bottle?
quiz.explanation: 1 litre = 1000 ml, so 10 ml costs 5000/1000*10 = 50 KES.

quiz.q: Why should you add a small percentage for waste when calculating cost per unit?
options: B) To account for spillage and errors
quiz.explanation: Waste percentage covers accidental loss during production.

quiz.q: For incense, if total materials cost 1,700 KES for 100 sticks, what is the cost per stick?
quiz.explanation: 1700 KES divided by 100 sticks = 17 KES per stick.

quiz.q: What is a common rule for setting wholesale price based on cost?
quiz.explanation: Wholesale is often set at double the cost per unit.

quiz.q: If cost per perfume oil is 200 KES, what is a typical retail price using the triple rule?
quiz.explanation: Triple cost means 200 x 3 = 600 KES.

quiz.q: Why might you offer a lower wholesale price for larger orders?
quiz.explanation: Bulk discounts incentivize customers to buy more.

quiz.q: What should you always ensure when setting a wholesale price?
options: A) It is higher than retail
B) It covers all costs and leaves profit
C) It is the same as retail
quiz.explanation: Wholesale price must be above total cost to be sustainable.

quiz.q: Which of these is considered packaging for perfume oils?
quiz.explanation: Bottle and label are packaging materials, not ingredients.

quiz.q: If you make 20 perfume oils in 2 hours and want to earn 200 KES per hour, what is labor cost per unit?
quiz.explanation: Total labor = 2 hours x 200 = 400 KES; per unit = 400/20 = 20 KES.

quiz.q: What is overhead?
options: B) Ongoing business expenses like rent and electricity
quiz.explanation: Overhead includes indirect costs not tied to a specific unit.

quiz.q: If monthly overhead is 10,000 KES and you produce 500 units, what is overhead per unit?
quiz.explanation: 10000 / 500 = 20 KES per unit.

quiz.q: Why is it important to include labor cost even if you work alone?
options: B) To value your time and ensure profit
quiz.explanation: Your time has value; ignoring it can lead to underpricing.

quiz.q: What is a break-even point?
options: A) When you make a profit
B) When total revenue equals total cost
C) When you sell at a loss
D) When you double your money
quiz.explanation: Break-even is the point of no profit or loss.

quiz.q: If cost per perfume oil is 330 KES, what is the minimum price you can sell at without losing money?
quiz.explanation: You cannot sell below cost without losing money.

quiz.q: What is a bulk deal?
options: A) Selling one item at a high price
B) Offering a discount for large quantity purchases
quiz.explanation: Bulk deals encourage larger orders by lowering unit price.

quiz.q: If retail price is 990 KES and you offer 20% off, what is the discounted price?
Why should you calculate profit margin before offering discounts?
options: A) To know how much discount you can afford
quiz.explanation: You need to ensure discounts don't eat into your profit.

quiz.q: What is a simple tool for tracking expenses?
quiz.explanation: A notebook is a basic, effective tool for recording expenses.

quiz.q: In a expense notebook, what columns should you have?
options: A) Date, Item, Cost, Quantity, Total
quiz.explanation: These columns capture necessary details for each expense.

quiz.q: Why is consistency important in tracking expenses?
options: A) To make the notebook look neat
B) To have accurate records for decision-making
quiz.explanation: Accurate records help you know your true costs and profits.

quiz.q: What can you use to track expenses digitally?
options: A) A smartphone app like Expense Manager
quiz.explanation: Apps like Expense Manager are designed for tracking expenses.

quiz.q: How often should you calculate your cost per unit?
options: B) Every month or when prices change
quiz.explanation: Regular updates ensure your pricing stays profitable.

quiz.q: What is profit margin?
options: B) Percentage of sale that is profit

Why might a business choose a lower margin, high volume strategy?
options: A) To make more profit per unit
B) To sell more units and still make good total profit
quiz.explanation: Selling more at lower margin can yield higher total profit.

quiz.q: What should you do with a portion of your profit for growth?
options: A) Spend it all on personal items
C) Save it under a mattress
quiz.explanation: Reinvesting profit helps the business expand and improve.

quiz.q: What is a good net profit margin target for a small business?
quiz.explanation: 20-30% is a healthy net profit margin for growth.

quiz.q: What can you do if your profit margin drops?
options: B) Find out why and adjust prices or cut costs
quiz.explanation: Analyzing the cause helps you take corrective action.
